pages.title: Northvale Rail: the road to 60 million journeys
pages.why: The deck's cover

pages.title: Northvale can reach 60 million journeys by FY31 by filling the off-peak
pages.why: The opening states the answer and the four levers behind it, each with the condition it depends on
pages.highlight: frequency, not fares, is the main lever

pages.title: The peak is full; the growth is in the hours between the peaks
pages.why: The whole plan turns on one observation, which deserves a page of its own before the evidence

pages.title: 01 / Where ridership stands
pages.why: Section structure

pages.title: Journeys recovered to 48 million but stalled 4 million below the FY20 peak
pages.why: The claim is the shape of the recovery - a steep rebound and then a plateau short of the FY20 peak - so the break and the stall are marked where they happen

pages.title: Peak trains run above 90% full on every line; off-peak trains run under half
pages.why: One question - how full are the trains - answered for the peak and the off-peak on the same five lines, side by side

pages.title: Northvale sits mid-table on journeys per route-km, 27% below the leading peer
pages.why: Where Northvale stands among all seven regional operators on one intensity measure is the claim, so the whole set is ranked and Northvale marked

pages.title: Leisure is two thirds of off-peak travel but only a seventh of the peak
pages.why: The claim is how the mix of trip purposes differs between the peak, the off-peak and the weekend, each resolving to 100%

pages.title: Half-hourly off-peak stations grew off-peak journeys 3.7 times as fast as hourly ones
pages.why: The claim is that two measures move together across the stations - off-peak frequency and off-peak growth - so each station is one point

pages.title: The Eastern line carries the most journeys at the highest cost per train-km
pages.why: Five measures per line are looked up and compared under their units, and no single chart would hold all five

pages.title: 02 / What holds it back
pages.why: Section structure

pages.title: Hybrid working cost 7.1 million journeys; housing and timetable changes won back 5.0 million
pages.why: The change from the FY20 peak to FY26 is made of five reconciled drivers, each of which the plan treats differently

pages.title: Each peak train added to the Eastern line has cost a point of punctuality
pages.why: Two measures of the same line over the same years - trains added and punctuality lost - only prove the claim read together

pages.title: Frequency drives a loop: shorter waits win leisure trips that fund the next train
pages.why: Off-peak growth is a loop in which each turn funds the next, so it is drawn as a cycle rather than a list
highlight: twice as often as the fare

pages.title: The Dales and Valley lines can grow now; the Coast line cannot
pages.why: Five lines are judged on the same four readiness criteria, and each line's verdict sits in its own row

pages.title: Passengers name the wait, not the fare, as what keeps them off trains
pages.why: Three survey findings each need their evidence and their consequence for the plan, one finding to a row

pages.title: Lapsed riders blame the hourly service, not the fare, for driving instead
pages.why: The survey finding is clearest in passengers' own words, so three voices from three corridors carry the page

pages.title: Three corridors serve three different markets, each needing its own timetable
pages.why: The three corridors are different places with different travellers, and the reader should see them before the plan treats them differently

pages.title: 03 / The plan
pages.why: Section structure

pages.title: Electrifying the Eastern line beats bi-mode trains on cost per journey from year six
pages.why: The Eastern line decision is between two options compared on the same four terms: cost, timing, running cost and what each frees up

pages.title: Four levers add 11.7 million journeys, led by the off-peak timetable
pages.why: The four levers are parallel and independent, each with its own size, owner and dependency, so they read as four columns

pages.title: London and Manchester send three in five of the visitors from beyond the network
pages.why: Where the visitors come from is the claim, so the origin cities are drawn on the map, sized by the journeys they send, with their routes into Leeds

pages.title: The plan adds 11.7 million journeys a year by FY31, mostly after electrification
pages.why: One number carries the plan - the journeys it adds - with the path to it underneath and the conditions beside it

pages.title: Fare revenue passes its FY20 level in FY29, carried by off-peak travel
pages.why: Revenue's path over eight years, split into peak and off-peak, shows both when it passes the FY20 level and which part does the work

pages.title: The plan costs £640 million, mostly in FY28-FY29, and pays back in eleven years
pages.why: The cost of the plan has three parts the reader needs together - when it is spent, on what, and how quickly it pays back

pages.title: Grant covers just over half the cost; Northvale must borrow or earn the rest
pages.why: The claim is what the £640 million of funding is made of, four parts of one total

pages.title: 04 / Delivering it
pages.why: Section structure

pages.title: Electrification sets the critical path; the off-peak timetable starts in 2027 regardless
pages.why: The question is what happens when, and which workstream the others wait on

pages.title: Four named owners carry one lever each, reporting monthly to the managing director
pages.why: Each lever has one accountable owner, and the reader needs to know who they are and what each is on the hook for

pages.title: Two of seven 2027 milestones are at risk, both on the electrification path
pages.why: Seven milestones are each judged on one criterion - on track or not - and the pattern of the red ones is the finding

pages.title: Service grows by a fifth while punctuality holds at 90% and unit cost falls
pages.why: Three numbers set the operating constraint the plan must hold, over the service growth that tests it

pages.title: Fare reform should follow the new timetable, not lead it
pages.why: The case for sequencing fares after the timetable is reasoning about cause and order, which reads best as prose

pages.title: Four decisions put Northvale on the path to 60 million journeys
pages.why: The close restates the answer as the decisions the board is asked to take
